notesStmt.note: This manuscript was almost certainly created sometime between August 5, 1888, the date of Sheridan's death, and August 12, 1888, when it was first published.

This poem first appeared, without title, in the 12 August 1888 issue of the New York Herald, at the head of the paper's coverage of General Philip Sheridan's funeral. For its reprinting in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891), Whitman restored the title and added both a headnote and a footnoote.

lg.head: Funeral Sounds not in interpolations
lg.l: Athwart the ‸Over and through the burial chant

Organ and solemn service, sermon, and
bending priests
‸To me Come stealing to me interpolation sounds not in the service here or in the show–
But winding ‸—plainly to me through ‸all the the heavy aisle and window ‸sounding

Of ‸active sudden battle's hurry, and harsh noises— war's, war's
grim game ‸to sight and ear in earnest

The scout brought call'd up & forward——the new-brought word—the
instantaneous order issued

The rifle⹀crack—the cannon thud—the
rushing forth of the companies ‸from their tents,

The clank of cavalry—the strange celerity
of the forming ranks,—the slender bugle-note

The noise of horses' hoofs ‸departing—saddles, arms,—accoutrements. and
arms.
